rounds.text: Southern Magnesium & Chemicals Ltd trades at a negative P/E of -76.09x, which stands in stark contrast to the sector benchmark of 18.54x [E5]. Furthermore, the company delivers a negative Return on Assets (ROA) of -1.5%, significantly trailing the sector benchmark of 4.72% [E7]. Profitability generation has severely deteriorated, with Return on Equity (ROE) dropping to a meager 0.97% against a sector benchmark of 7.82% [E8], matching the filed statement figure of 1.0% [E12] and the one-year median ROE of 1% [E28]. Investors receive zero compensation for holding this risk, as evidenced by a dividend yield of 0.00% [E3]. Compounding these fundamental weaknesses, the stock languishes near the bottom of its yearly performance, sitting merely 13% of the way up its 52-week range between a 61 low and 131 high [E4]. Conceded: the company demonstrates a strong historical return on equity track record, with a 10-year median ROE of 25% [E25], a 5-year median ROE of 27% [E26], a 3-year median ROE of 21% [E27], and positive flags regarding its 3-year ROE of 20.6% [E53].

Conceded: the company currently displays a negative P/E of -76.09x versus the sector benchmark of 18.54x [E5], a negative ROA of -1.5% compared to the 4.72% sector benchmark [E7], and an ROE of 0.97% to 1.0% matching the one-year median of 1% [E3, E8, E12, E28]. Conceded: the dividend yield stands at 0.00% [E3] and the stock sits at just 13% of its 52-week range [E4]. However, these short-term cyclical dips completely ignore a proven, elite multi-year compounding engine demonstrated by a 10-year median ROE of 25%, a 5-year median ROE of 27%, and a 3-year median ROE of 21% [E25, E26, E27, E53]. This historical earning power is available at a modest price-to-book of 1.61x—cheaper than the sector benchmark of 2.15x [E6]—on a book value of ₹ 43.5 [E1]. With a microscopic market capitalisation of only ₹ 21.0 Cr [E2], the current pessimism is severely overdone relative to the company's established ability to generate high returns across extended periods.

Conceded: the company boasts a 10-year median ROE of 25%, a 5-year median ROE of 27%, and a 3-year median ROE of 21% [E25, E26, E27]. However, the bull's reliance on historical compounding collapses when confronted with the reality that the most recent 1-year median ROE has cratered to a mere 1% [E28], aligning directly with the current annual ROE of 0.97% to 1.0% [E8, E12]. This steep deceleration proves that past multi-year medians [E25, E26, E27, E53] are stale and fail to reflect the company's severely degraded present earning power. Furthermore, the claim that a 1.61x price-to-book ratio [E1, E6] offers cheap access to this earnings engine is hollow when the business is actively generating a negative ROA of -1.5% against a sector benchmark of 4.72% [E7]. A micro-cap valuation of ₹ 21.0 Cr [E2] and a stock languishing at 13% of its 52-week range [E4] with a 0.00% dividend yield [E3] do not represent temporary pessimism, but rather a rational market response to an unravelling operational profile carrying a staggering negative P/E of -76.09x [E5].
